examples.en: The court dismissed the lawsuit.

examples.ko: 재판부는 서류가 부족하다며 신청을 각하할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The court can dismiss the petition, saying documents are missing.

examples.ko: 관청에서 제 신청을 각하해서 다시 접수했어요.
examples.en: The office turned down my application, so I filed it again.

examples.ko: 법원이 청구를 각하하면 이유를 알려 줘요.
examples.en: When the court dismisses a claim, it tells you the reason.
The committee decided to dismiss that request.
The judge explained why he dismissed it.

explain: 법원이나 관청이 신청이나 소송을 내용 판단 없이 돌려보낼 때 써요. 일상에서 거절할 때는 '거절하다'나 '안 받아 주다'를 쓰고, '각하하다'는 법률 뉴스에서만 거의 나와요.

phrases.en: The court did not dismiss that application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 법원이 신청을 돌려보내지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning the court did not turn the application away.

phrases.en: The court made a decision to dismiss it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사 '각하'를 써서 결과를 알리는 뉴스 말투예요. '결정을 내리다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun form in a news style to report the result, usually with 'make a decision'.

phrases.en: The office dismissed the application form that was past its deadline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소송뿐 아니라 관청에 낸 서류에도 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing showing the verb is used for papers submitted to an office, not only lawsuits.

explain_en: Used when a court or office returns a petition or lawsuit without ruling on its merits. In daily life you'd say 거절하다 for refusing; 각하하다 appears almost only in legal news.

examples.en: The company pushed ahead with the new construction as planned.
We'll go ahead with the event even if it rains.
The committee decided to force the vote through despite objections.
If you push through a schedule too hard, your health suffers.
They say the government is forcing the new policy through.

examples.ko: 피곤하면 강행하지 말고 하루 더 쉬어요.
examples.en: If you're tired, don't push on; rest one more day.

explain: 반대가 있거나 어려운 상황인데도 그대로 밀어붙이는 느낌이라 좋은 뜻으로는 잘 안 써요. '진행하다'는 그냥 이어서 하는 말이라 이런 느낌이 없어요. '공사를 강행하다', '출발을 강행하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The company decided to push ahead with the launch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대가 있어도 그대로 하기로 결정했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means deciding to go ahead despite opposition.

phrases.en: Don't force yourself to work when you're sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무리해서 밀어붙이지 말라고 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone not to push on against the odds.

phrases.en: He forced the schedule through unreasonably.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무리하게'가 붙으면 좋지 않은 결과가 걱정되는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: '무리하게' adds a sense of worry about bad results.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of pressing on despite opposition or difficulty, so it isn't usually positive. 진행하다 just means carrying on and has no such edge. It takes an object, as in '공사를 강행하다' and '출발을 강행하다'.

examples.en: My parents don't interfere in my affairs.

examples.ko: 그 사건에 관여한 사람들이 조사를 받았어요.
examples.en: The people involved in that case were investigated.
The boss got directly involved in the work and made the decision.
The government is stepping in on prices.

examples.ko: 저는 그 문제에 관여할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't get involved in that matter.
I don't know how far I'm allowed to get involved.

explain: '관여하다'는 어떤 일에 관계를 맺고 끼어든다는 느낌이고, 보통 '일에 관여하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 모임이나 행사에 같이 하는 '참여하다'와 달리, 남의 일이나 결정에 개입한다는 느낌이 있어서 부정문에 자주 나와요. 더 강하게 나서는 '간섭하다'보다는 중립적이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 그 문제에 관여하고 싶지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't want to get involved in that problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 일에 끼어들고 싶지 않을 때 쓰는 자연스러운 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural negative phrase for not wanting to step into someone else's matter.
phrases.en_equiv: to not want to get involved

phrases.example: 그 사람이 이 일에 깊이 관여했어요.
phrases.en: That person was deeply involved in this matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깊이'를 붙이면 단순한 관계가 아니라 많이 개입했다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '깊이' means heavy involvement, not just a connection.

phrases.example: 회사 결정에는 제가 관여할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: I can't get involved in the company's decisions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권한이 없어서 끼어들 수 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have no authority to step in.

explain_en: 관여하다 means to step into and have a hand in something, and it is usually paired with 에, as in 일에 관여하다. Unlike 참여하다, which means joining a meeting or event, 관여하다 has the sense of getting involved in someone else's matter or decision, so it often appears in negative sentences. It is more neutral than the stronger 간섭하다 (to meddle).

examples.en: The baby shakes its head to say no.
I asked my friend for a favor, but all he did was shake his head.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹이면 아기가 도리질을 치며 입을 다물어요.
examples.en: When I try to feed the baby, it shakes its head and shuts its mouth.

examples.ko: 모두 찬성했는데 한 사람만 도리질을 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone agreed, but one person shook his head.

examples.ko: 도리질 한 번에 제 제안은 거절당했어요.
examples.en: With a single shake of the head, my suggestion was turned down.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 도리질로 대답했어요.
examples.en: He answered with a shake of the head, without saying a word.

explain: 보통 '도리질을 하다/치다'로 쓰고, 싫다거나 아니라는 뜻으로 고개를 좌우로 흔드는 동작이에요. 어린아이의 모습을 말할 때 특히 잘 어울려요. 어른에게는 '고개를 젓다'가 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.example: 아기가 밥을 안 먹겠다고 도리질을 해요.
phrases.en: The baby shakes her head, refusing to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 아이가 싫다고 고개를 흔드는 모습에 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, fitting a child shaking her head to say no.

phrases.example: 동생은 병원에 가자고 하니까 도리질을 쳤어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling shook his head when I said let's go to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'보다 고개를 더 힘차게 흔드는 느낌이 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like a more vigorous head shake than 하다.

phrases.example: 그는 제 말을 듣고 조용히 고개를 저었어요.
phrases.en: He listened to me and quietly shook his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이나 일반 상황에서는 이 말이 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: For adults or general situations, this is more everyday.

explain_en: It is usually used as '도리질을 하다/치다' and means shaking your head side to side to say no. It fits especially well when describing small children. For adults, '고개를 젓다' is more everyday.

examples.ko: 그 일은 뒤탈 없이 잘 마무리됐어요.
examples.en: That matter was wrapped up well without any trouble afterward.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 나서 뒤탈이 생길까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that I might get side effects after taking the medicine.

examples.ko: 돈 문제는 미리 정해 놓아야 뒤탈이 없어요.
examples.en: You have to settle money matters in advance to avoid trouble later.

examples.ko: 이렇게 하면 나중에 뒤탈이 날 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you do it this way, there could be trouble later.

examples.ko: 상한 음식을 먹었는데 다행히 뒤탈은 없었어요.
examples.en: I ate spoiled food, but luckily I had no bad after-effects.
Check the contract carefully so there's no trouble later.

explain: 일이 끝난 뒤에 생기는 말썽이나, 음식·약을 먹은 뒤에 몸에 생기는 탈을 말해요. '뒤탈이 없다, 뒤탈이 생기다, 뒤탈이 나다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 계약서를 꼼꼼히 써 두면 뒤탈이 없어요.
phrases.en: If you write the contract carefully, there won't be trouble later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 문제가 생기지 않는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means no problems will come up later.

phrases.en: I ate spoiled food and got sick afterward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 약을 먹고 나서 배탈 같은 문제가 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a problem like an upset stomach appeared after eating or taking medicine.

phrases.example: 약을 같이 먹어도 되는지 뒤탈이 걱정돼요.
phrases.en: I'm worried about side effects of taking the medicines together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 생길 문제를 미리 걱정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when worrying ahead of time about later problems.

explain_en: It refers to trouble that appears after something is over, or to a bad reaction in the body after eating food or taking medicine. It is commonly used as '뒤탈이 없다', '뒤탈이 생기다' and '뒤탈이 나다'.

en: to be awkward or improper to say/do; to be hesitant

examples.ko: 이 일을 제가 직접 말하기가 좀 무엇해요.
examples.en: It's a bit awkward for me to say this directly.
It's a bit awkward to call at this late hour.
It was awkward to refuse, so I just went.
It feels awkward to talk about money with a friend.
It's a bit awkward to be the one who contacts first.
If it's awkward, let's talk again next time.

explain: '말하기 무엇하다'처럼 하기 곤란하거나 어색한 걸 돌려 말할 때 써요. 말하는 사람이 일부러 말끝을 흐리는 느낌이에요. '곤란하다', '어색하다'보다 부드럽고, 주로 '~기가 무엇하다' 틀로 써요.

phrases.en: It feels a bit awkward to ask right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무엇하다'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 무엇하다, used more in speech.

phrases.example: 이런 말은 무엇하지만 이 음식은 좀 짜요.
phrases.en: I hate to say it, but this food is a bit salty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하기 조심스러운 이야기를 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to begin something that feels delicate to say.
phrases.en_equiv: I hate to say it, but

phrases.en: It's a bit difficult to say here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무엇하다'보다 곤란한 이유가 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes the difficulty clearer than 무엇하다.

explain_en: Used to indirectly say something is awkward or hard to do, as in '말하기 무엇하다'. The speaker softens the sentence on purpose. It is gentler than '곤란하다' or '어색하다' and mostly appears in the pattern '~기가 무엇하다'.

en: to be deferred; to be put off

examples.en: That agenda item was put on hold at the meeting.

examples.ko: 예산 문제로 공사 계획이 보류되고 있어요.
examples.en: The construction plan is on hold because of budget issues.
The schedule slipped because the decision was put on hold.

examples.ko: 신청서가 보류되어 있는 이유를 알고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to know why my application is on hold.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 출발이 보류될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If it rains a lot, the departure may be put on hold.
The project that had been put on hold will start again.

explain: 보류되다는 결정을 하지 않고 뒤로 남겨 둔다는 느낌이라 아예 없애는 '취소'와 달라요. 회의, 심사, 행정 장면에서 많이 나와요. '미뤄지다'는 날짜가 늦춰질 때, 보류되다는 판단 자체를 나중에 할 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: The final decision was put off until the next meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의나 심사에서 결정을 나중으로 남겨 둘 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for leaving a decision for later in meetings or reviews.

phrases.en: My application is still on hold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 결정이 멈춰 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a decision is currently on hold.

phrases.en: The event date was postponed because of rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보류되다'가 판단을 나중에 한다는 뜻이라면, '미뤄지다'는 날짜나 일정이 늦춰질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 보류되다 means the judgment is left for later, 미뤄지다 is for dates or schedules being delayed.

explain_en: This means a decision is left undecided for later, which is different from '취소' (cancellation), where it is dropped completely. It is common in meetings, screenings, and administration. '미뤄지다' fits when a date is pushed back, while '보류되다' fits when the judgment itself waits.

examples.en: The company put the launch of the new product on hold.

examples.ko: 일단 결정을 보류하고 더 생각해 볼게요.
examples.en: Let me hold off on deciding and think about it more.
The judges decided to withhold their judgment.

examples.ko: 급하지 않으면 구매를 보류하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If it is not urgent, it is better to hold off on buying.
We will leave that issue pending until the next meeting.
I left without giving an answer.

explain: 보류하다는 결정이나 처리를 하지 않고 남겨 두는 것이라서 '취소하다'와 달리 나중에 다시 다룰 여지가 있어요. 공식적인 자리에서 '결정을 보류하다', '판단을 보류하다'로 자주 써요. 가볍게는 '미루다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I held off on judging because there wasn't enough information.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결론을 내리지 않고 더 지켜볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for not reaching a conclusion yet and waiting to see more.

phrases.en: I'll put that agenda item on hold for now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 다시 다룰 생각으로 잠시 놓아둔다는 느낌의 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form with the feel of setting something aside to deal with later.

phrases.en: I put off today's decision until tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보류하다'보다 가볍고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter than 보류하다 and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: This means leaving a decision or action undone, so unlike '취소하다' (cancel), it can be taken up again later. In formal settings it appears as '결정을 보류하다' (hold off on a decision) or '판단을 보류하다' (withhold judgment). In casual speech, '미루다' (put off) is used.

examples.en: I offered coffee, but they said no thanks and declined.
I'll accept the thought but politely decline the gift.
I'll help you. Please don't hold back.

examples.ko: 그분은 큰 상을 사양하고 조용히 떠났어요.
examples.en: He turned down the big prize and left quietly.
I tried to give up my seat, but the grandmother politely declined.

examples.ko: 너무 사양할 필요 없어요. 많이 드세요!
examples.en: No need to be so shy about it. Eat a lot!

explain: '사양하다'는 상대의 호의를 정중하게 거절할 때 써요. '거절하다'보다 부드럽고 예의가 있어요. 한국에서는 음식이나 선물을 권하면 처음엔 '괜찮아요' 하고 사양하는 일이 많아서, 권하는 쪽은 한 번 더 권해요.

phrases.en: I'll pass on the alcohol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권하는 것을 정중하게 거절할 때 바로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A direct, polite way to turn down an offer.

phrases.en: Don't be shy. Please eat a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님에게 부담 갖지 말고 편하게 하라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to urge a guest not to hold back.

phrases.en: He politely declined the invitation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의를 지키며 거절하는 모습을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses declining while staying courteous.

explain_en: 사양하다 is used to politely decline someone's kindness. It's softer and more courteous than 거절하다. In Korea, people often decline food or gifts at first with 괜찮아요, so the person offering usually offers once more.

p.n: 거절하다 is a plain 'no'; 사양하다 sounds more modest and polite.

en: to repay; to pay back; to return

examples.en: I am paying back my loan a little each month.
It takes five years to repay all of the tuition loan.

examples.ko: 회사는 빌린 돈을 약속한 날짜에 상환했어요.
examples.en: The company repaid the borrowed money on the promised date.
Can you pay off the debt all at once?

examples.ko: 이자와 원금을 나누어 상환하는 방법도 있어요.
examples.en: There is also a way to repay the interest and principal in parts.

examples.ko: 먼저 카드 대금을 상환해야 새 카드를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to settle your card balance first to get a new card.

explain: 친구에게 빌린 돈은 '갚다', 은행 대출이나 채무는 '상환하다'를 써요. 보통 '대출금을 상환하다', '빚을 상환하다'처럼 목적어가 돈이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '갚다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I paid back all the money I borrowed from the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '상환하다'보다 이 말이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural than 상환하다 in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I'm going to repay my debt within this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적어가 '빚'일 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing where the object is debt.

phrases.example: 돈이 없어서 대출금을 상환할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: I have no money, so I can't repay the loan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갚을 능력이 없을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is unable to pay back what they owe.

explain_en: For money borrowed from a friend, Koreans say '갚다'; for bank loans and debts they use '상환하다'. The object is usually money, as in '대출금을 상환하다'. In everyday conversation '갚다' sounds much more natural.

examples.en: When I gave her a gift, my grandmother waved her hand to refuse.
It was cute to see him wave his hand and say it was fine.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 저도 모르게 손사래가 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I heard that, I waved my hands without realizing it.
He showed his refusal by waving his hand.

examples.ko: 식당 주인이 손사래까지 치며 돈을 안 받으셨어요.
examples.en: The restaurant owner even waved me off and wouldn't take my money.

examples.ko: 손사래만 치고 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: She only waved her hand and didn't say anything.

explain: 주로 '손사래를 치다'로 쓰고, 손을 내저으며 싫다, 아니다, 괜찮다고 표현할 때 써요. 인사로 손을 흔드는 것과는 달라서 '손을 흔들다'와 바꿔 쓰면 안 돼요. 사양하거나 부인하는 장면에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Grandmother waved her hands and said it was fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손을 내저으면서 다른 말을 이어서 할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used when you say something while waving your hands in refusal.

phrases.example: 손사래 치지 마시고 한번 드셔 보세요.
phrases.en: Please don't wave it away, and just try it once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 사양할 때 정중하게 권하면서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite phrase used when offering something to someone who keeps refusing.

phrases.en: He waved his hand to say no.
phrases.nuance_ko: '손사래를 치다'와 거의 같은 뜻인데 동작을 직접 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 'make a hand-waving gesture', but it describes the action directly.
phrases.en_equiv: to wave one's hand side to side

explain_en: It is mostly used as '손사래를 치다', meaning to wave one's hands to say no, deny something or politely decline. It is not the same as waving hello or goodbye, so it can't be swapped with '손을 흔들다'. It often appears in scenes of refusing or denying.

examples.ko: 이 일은 쉬이 끝나지 않을 것 같아요.
examples.en: This work doesn't look like it will end easily.
The memory of that day isn't easily forgotten.

examples.ko: 쉬이 포기하지 말고 한 번 더 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't give up so easily; try one more time.
You shouldn't believe it that readily.

examples.ko: 쉬이 잠이 오지 않아서 밤새 뒤척였어요.
examples.en: I couldn't fall asleep easily and tossed and turned all night.

examples.ko: 쉬이 구할 수 있는 재료로 만든 음식이에요.
examples.en: It's a dish made with ingredients that are easy to get.

explain: '쉽게'와 같은 뜻이지만 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말투에서 더 어울려요. 뒤에 '않다, 못하다' 같은 부정 표현이 자주 와요. 말할 때는 보통 '쉽게'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 첫 여행의 기억은 쉬이 잊히지 않아요.
phrases.en: The memory of my first trip is not easily forgotten.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쉬이' 뒤에 부정 표현이 오는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern, with a negative expression after 쉬이.

phrases.en: He is a person who doesn't give up easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈기 있는 사람을 글처럼 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a written-style description of a persistent person.

phrases.example: 이 문제는 쉽게 풀 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can solve this problem easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이지만 말할 때는 '쉬이'보다 '쉽게'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 쉽게 is far more common in speech.

explain_en: It means the same as '쉽게' but fits writing or a slightly formal tone better. It is often followed by negatives such as '않다' or '못하다'. In speech people usually just say '쉽게'.

en: to approve; to consent; to permit

examples.en: My parents agreed to my studying abroad.
The boss approved my vacation request.
She gladly agreed to my request.
After thinking about it for a long time, I decided to agree.

examples.ko: 그는 결혼 제안을 승낙할 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems he will accept the marriage proposal.

examples.ko: 제가 먼저 부탁했는데 상대방이 승낙하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I asked first, but the other person didn't consent.

explain: '허락하다'와 비슷하지만 '승낙하다'는 부탁이나 요청을 받아들여 '좋다'고 답한다는 느낌이 강해요. 윗사람이나 회사처럼 결정하는 쪽의 대답으로 자주 나와요. 친구끼리는 보통 '좋아', '그래'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I got my parents' consent for the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁한 일에 대해 허락을 얻었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting approval for something you asked for.

phrases.en: The teacher agreed to my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방이 부탁을 들어줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone grants your request.

phrases.en: My father allowed my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승낙하다'와 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '승낙하다' but used more often in daily talk.

explain_en: Close to 허락하다, but 승낙하다 stresses accepting a request and answering yes. It often describes the reply from someone with the authority to decide, like a boss or company. Between friends people just say 좋아 or 그래.

dis.h: formal; agree to a request or proposal

p.n: The other word is plainer and means giving permission.

examples.en: The celebrity apologized and went into a period of lying low.
Right now I need time for self-reflection and restraint.

examples.ko: 자숙 기간이 끝나면 다시 활동할 거예요.
examples.en: When the lying-low period ends, he will resume activities.

examples.ko: 그는 사고 이후 자숙하며 조용히 지냈어요.
examples.en: After the accident, he kept a low profile and stayed quiet.

examples.ko: 모두가 힘든 때라 파티는 자숙하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Since everyone is having a hard time, we decided to hold back on the party.
The city hall asked citizens to refrain from going out.

explain: 잘못이 있거나 분위기가 무거울 때 스스로 말과 행동을 조심하고 활동을 줄이는 것을 말해요. 뉴스에서 '자숙 기간, 자숙하다'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 잘못을 한 선수는 한동안 자숙해야 해요.
phrases.en: A player who did wrong must keep a low profile for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자숙'을 동사로 쓴 말이고 조심하며 활동을 줄인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to be careful and cut back on activities.

phrases.example: 자숙 기간이 끝나고 다시 방송에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: After the period of self-restraint ended, he appeared on TV again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 연예인이나 정치인의 사건을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in news about celebrities or politicians.

phrases.en: That actor is currently keeping a low profile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 조심하며 활동을 쉬고 있다는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current state of laying low.

explain_en: It means holding back on your words and actions yourself after a mistake or when the mood is heavy. In the news you often hear '자숙 기간' and '자숙하다'.

examples.ko: 두 의견을 절충해서 새로운 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: We combined the two opinions and made a new plan.
I talked with the owner to settle on a price in the middle.
Let's each give a little and try to meet in the middle.
It took a long time in the process of finding a middle ground.

examples.ko: 우리 의견을 절충한 결과가 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the result of merging our opinions.

examples.ko: 그 가게의 인기 메뉴는 한식과 양식을 절충했어요.
examples.en: That shop's popular menu item blends Korean and Western food.

explain: 서로 다른 두 가지의 좋은 점을 섞어서 가운데쯤의 안을 만든다는 느낌이에요. '타협하다'는 서로 양보해서 합의한다는 쪽에 가깝고, '절충하다'는 두 가지를 섞은 새 안을 만든다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 두 팀이 서로 받아들일 수 있는 절충안을 내놓았어요.
phrases.en: The two teams came up with a compromise that both could accept.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 두 의견을 섞어 만든 가운데쯤의 안을 말해요. 보통 '절충안을 내다/찾다'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A middle-ground plan made by mixing two different opinions. Usually 절충안을 내다/찾다.

phrases.en: We each gave a little and reached a compromise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말인데 서로 양보해서 합의한다는 쪽에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that leans more toward both sides giving in and reaching agreement.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 의견을 끝내 절충하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: The two people were never able to find a compromise between their views.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 못하다'를 붙여서 가운데 안을 만들지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -지 못하다 it means they could not work out a middle position.

explain_en: It feels like mixing the good points of two different things into a middle option. '타협하다' leans toward reaching agreement by both giving way, while '절충하다' more strongly suggests making a new plan that blends the two.

examples.en: The company withdrew the plan it announced yesterday.
I asked them to retract the incorrect article.
The government will withdraw the new policy.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 화가 나서 지원을 철회했어요.
examples.en: He was angry and withdrew his support.
Where do I go to withdraw my application?
The backlash was strong, so he took back his remark and apologized.

explain: 철회하다는 이미 내놓은 주장, 신청, 계획을 거두어들일 때 써요. 신청서나 정책, 발언처럼 공식적인 것에 주로 쓰고, 일상 약속에는 '취소하다'를 더 많이 써요. '발언을 철회하다'는 말한 내용을 없던 것으로 하겠다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Something came up, so I withdrew my application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 낸 신청서를 거두어들일 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for taking back an application you've already submitted.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 어제 한 발언을 철회했어요.
phrases.en: He took back the remarks he made yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말한 내용을 없던 것으로 하겠다고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone formally says that what they said should be treated as unsaid.

phrases.en: Citizens demanded that the policy be withdrawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '철회'로 쓰면 뉴스에서 정책이나 결정을 거두라고 요구하는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a noun, '철회' appears in news about demanding that a policy or decision be withdrawn.

explain_en: 철회하다 is for pulling back something you already put forward, such as an application, a policy, or a statement. It sounds official; for everyday plans Koreans say '취소하다' instead. '발언을 철회하다' means treating what you said as unsaid.

dis.h: take back a statement, plan or decision

p.n: 취하하다 is for lawsuits and applications, so it is not natural with a plan.

examples.en: Famous actors have very high appearance fees.

examples.ko: 영화 출연료를 받고 가족과 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: I got my film appearance fee and went on a trip with my family.

examples.ko: 신인 가수는 출연료가 거의 없다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a rookie singer gets almost no appearance fee.
We disagreed with the broadcaster over the appearance fee.
The appearance fee is calculated per episode.
I donated the whole appearance fee I received at the event.

explain: 방송, 영화, 공연에 나온 대가를 말해요. 강의는 '강연료', 글은 '원고료'처럼 일에 따라 이름이 달라요. '출연료를 받다/주다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I received my drama appearance fee today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이나 영화에 나온 대가를 받는다는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for being paid for a show or film.

phrases.en: New actors get a small appearance fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금액이 낮다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the amount is low.

phrases.en: That actor donated their appearance fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 돈을 좋은 일에 내놓을 때 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often in news when the money is given to a good cause.

explain_en: It is the pay for appearing in a broadcast, film, or show. The fee name changes with the work: 강연료 for lectures, 원고료 for writing. You say 출연료를 받다 or 출연료를 주다.

examples.ko: 학교에서 오늘 아침에 합격 결과를 통보했어요.
examples.en: The school notified us of the admission result this morning.
The company informs employees of the moving date.
It is a problem if they suddenly announce that the contract is over.
We will notify you of the exam result by email.
Telling people in a one-sided way is not good.

examples.ko: 병원에서 검사 결과를 통보하고 나서 약을 처방했어요.
examples.en: After giving the test result, the hospital prescribed medicine.

explain: 결정된 사실을 공식적으로 알려 줄 때 써요. '알려 주다'와 달리 상대 의견을 묻지 않고 결과만 전하는 느낌이 강해요. '일방적으로 통보하다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The company unilaterally notified us that the contract was ending.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일방적으로'를 붙여 상대 의견을 묻지 않았다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '일방적으로' makes clear that the other side's opinion was not asked.

phrases.en: I received notice of my acceptance yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알림을 받는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who receives the notice.

phrases.en: I'll let you know the result by email.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통보하다'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than '통보하다' and used widely in daily life.

explain_en: Use it to officially announce something already decided. Unlike '알려 주다', it strongly suggests passing on only the result without asking the other person's opinion. A common phrase is '일방적으로 통보하다' (to notify one-sidedly).

examples.ko: 회원권 갱신 기간을 놓쳐서 다시 가입해야 한대요.
examples.en: I missed the membership renewal period, so I have to sign up again.
I signed up for a three-month gym membership.

examples.ko: 이 회원권으로 수영장도 쓸 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I use the pool with this membership too?
A friend passed on the membership he had been using to me.
If you have a membership, admission is half price.

examples.ko: 회원권 가격이 너무 비싸서 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: The membership price is so high that I'm still deciding.

explain: 시설을 이용할 수 있는 권리를 말해요. 회원임을 보여 주는 카드인 '회원증'과 달라요. 헬스장이나 수영장에서는 '회원권을 끊다'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The annual membership is cheaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일 년 동안 쓸 수 있는 회원권이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A membership valid for one year.

phrases.en: I extended my pool membership by one month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기간을 더 늘릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making the period longer.

phrases.en: I got a refund on my gym membership because I moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낸 돈을 돌려받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting your money back.

explain_en: It means the right to use a facility. It differs from '회원증', the card that shows you are a member. At gyms and pools, people often say '회원권을 끊다' for signing up.
